all_tweets.title:
Another $100M just went into institutional crypto infrastructure.

@tether invested $100M in @Anchor
all_tweets.description:
Another $100M just went into institutional crypto infrastructure.

@tether invested $100M in @Anchorage. This follows its earlier investment in @t0network.

Anchorage is the first federally regulated digital asset bank in the U.S. It provides custody, staking, settlement, and stablecoin services for institutions.

Tether already works with Anchorage to issue $USDT in the U.S., so this move deepens an existing partnership and strengthens the regulated banking layer behind USDT.

When you zoom out, the strategy becomes clear.

Anchorage handles regulated custody.
t0 focuses on tokenized settlement rails.

Together, these moves push USDT deeper into traditional finance infrastructure.

It's a meaningful step for crypto toward deeper institutional adoption.
A step that can have a long-term impact on this space.

XDC Network は、@BitGo によるインスティテューショナル・カストディのサポートを確保しました。これにより、XDC およびネットワーク上の USDC に対する規制準拠のカストディ環境が提供されます。
BitGo Bank & Trust を通じた規制下の MPC カストディにより、企業、取引所、金融機関は、貿易金融、決済、RWA（実世界資産）のトークン化領域でオンチェーンに資本を展開するために必要なセキュリティおよびコンプライアンス基盤へアクセス可能となります。

all_tweets.title: Sé que con BTC en $70K y el 97% de altcoins en rojo es difícil ver más allá. Pero lo que está pasand
all_tweets.description:
Sé que con BTC en $70K y el 97% de altcoins en rojo es difícil ver más allá. Pero lo que está pasando debajo del ruido de precios es, posiblemente, lo más importante del ciclo.

Anchorage Digital, el único banco con licencia federal cripto en EEUU (respaldado Goldman,Visa...), acaba de integrar acceso directo a Morpho, Aave, Lido y más de 50 protocolos DeFi a través de su wallet institucional. 

Hasta ahora, un fondo de pensiones o una tesorería corporativa que quisiera yield en DeFi tenía un problema serio: no podían. Su compliance se lo prohibía. Al no haber custodio instucional, era imposible.

Ese muro se está cayendo. Coinbase ya lanzó préstamos respaldados por crypto via Morpho. Bitwise, con $15B bajo gestión, ya es vault curator en Morpho ofreciendo ~6% APY en stablecoins. https://t.co/OmmZujUOBy integró lending via Morpho. Y ahora Anchorage abre la puerta a todo su libro de clientes institucionales.

Los números de Morpho hablan solos: de 67K a 1.4M usuarios en 2025, depósitos de $5B a $13B, préstamos activos en $4.5B, y $400M en RWAs tokenizados. Es el segundo protocolo de lending más grande, ya en 29 cadenas.

Como siempre, el capital institucional no llega en ATH cuando todo el mundo mira. Llega en silencio, a través de infraestructura regulada, custodia cualificada y productos que encajan con sus mandatos de compliance. Eso es exactamente lo que se está construyendo ahora.

Los precios nos están diciendo que cripto está muerto. 

La infraestructura nos está diciendo que es el mejor momento para encontrar proyectos ganadores.

all_tweets.title:
1. The Core Philosophy: "Bitcoin Stays Blind"

In standard bridges (like WBTC), there is a "Multisig
all_tweets.description:
1. The Core Philosophy: "Bitcoin Stays Blind"

In standard bridges (like WBTC), there is a "Multisig Wallet" on the Bitcoin network controlled by 5-10 entities (like BitGo). You have to trust them.

Alienc0der is saying: "Bitcoin should not verify the other chain (Zenon). Bitcoin must remain blind."
To the Bitcoin network, the transaction looks like a standard signature spend. Bitcoin does not say, "This transaction happened because tokens were burned on Zenon"; it simply says, "The signature is valid, transaction approved."

2. What is Witness Encryption?

This is the heart of the system.

Normally, to encrypt data, you need a Person (Public Key).

In Witness Encryption, you encrypt data to a Fact (NP Statement).

Example: I put Bitcoin in a box and program the lock as follows: "This lock will open if and only if a 'Burn Proof' (Witness) containing a specific transaction hash from the Zenon Network is presented."

The thing that opens the box is not a "Person" (Admin, Multisig member), but a Mathematical Proof.If that proof (Witness) exists, the encryption dissolves, and the Bitcoin is released. If the proof doesn't exist, all the computers in the universe combined cannot move that Bitcoin.

3. The Two Variants

Alienc0der mentions two different implementation methods here:

Variant A (Recommended - Signature Release):

Here, the "Private Key" is not encrypted.
Instead, the Signature of a pre-constructed Bitcoin transaction is encrypted.

Scenario: User burns zBTC on Zenon -> Generates Proof (Witness) -> Uses this proof to decrypt the package -> The package reveals only the signature required to execute that specific transaction.

Security: Even if the person decrypting it is malicious, the revealed signature only says "Send 1 BTC to User X." They cannot change it to "Send to User Y." At worst, they broadcast the transaction for everyone (which is what you want anyway).

Variant B (Obfuscated Contract):

A more complex method involving an "Obfuscated Smart Contract" (Smart Secret) that never reveals the key but outputs the signature. This is discussed more in Ethereum research circles (Suegami's research), but Variant A is cleaner and safer for Zenon.

4. The Implication for Zenon: "Programmability in Cryptography"

Alienc0der’s following sentence is critical:

"Programmability lives in cryptography, not Script"

Bitcoin's language (Script) is constrained ("No loops, no smart contracts"). Bitcoin L2s usually say, "Then let's change Bitcoin" (OP_CAT, covenants, etc.). Zenon says, "No, leave Bitcoin alone. We will embed the programmability into the Cryptography (Witness Encryption)."

In Summary: 
With this system, Zenon aims to become the first network to manage Bitcoin without the need for a Custodian. 
To convert Bitcoin to Zenon (zBTC), you don't trust a company; you trust mathematics (encrypted witness). If you burn zBTC on Zenon, the lock on the Bitcoin network opens automatically. There is no human in the middle, only the Witness.

Today, BDIC Insurance introduces a comprehensive crypto insurance framework built specifically for the emerging agentic AI payment economy.

• Smart contract and oracle failures

Built on BDIC’s decentralized insurance architecture, including our dual-tier risk framework and 33% reserve structure  , AgentCover Pro extends our mission of protecting digital assets into the next phase of blockchain adoption.

This is not speculation. It is infrastructure for programmable finance.

The digital dollar is the backbone of the ecosystem being built by the $WLFI team.

Its flagship pro
company.description:
The digital dollar is the backbone of the ecosystem being built by the $WLFI team.

Its flagship product is a fully backed 1:1 USD-pegged stablecoin, anchored to the U.S. dollar and supported by U.S. Treasuries, held under top-tier institutional custody with BitGo.

But the real differentiation goes beyond structure — it’s transparency.

All reserves are backed by monthly third-party attestations. While some competitors provide annual reports or simple self-disclosures, $WLFI raises the standard with frequent, independently verified certifications.

In addition, they were the first stablecoin to implement real-time, on-chain proof of reserves powered by Chainlink, allowing anyone in the world to verify where reserves are held and confirm that every dollar is fully backed.

Verifiable transparency. Institutional-grade security. Trust built on data.

Beyond the technology, let the numbers speak.

@tether invested $100M in @Anchor
company.description:
Another $100M just went into institutional crypto infrastructure.

@tether invested $100M in @Anchorage. This follows its earlier investment in @t0network.

Anchorage is the first federally regulated digital asset bank in the U.S. It provides custody, staking, settlement, and stablecoin services for institutions.

Tether already works with Anchorage to issue $USDT in the U.S., so this move deepens an existing partnership and strengthens the regulated banking layer behind USDT.

When you zoom out, the strategy becomes clear.

Anchorage handles regulated custody.
t0 focuses on tokenized settlement rails.

Together, these moves push USDT deeper into traditional finance infrastructure.

It's a meaningful step for crypto toward deeper institutional adoption.
A step that can have a long-term impact on this space.

company.title: Sé que con BTC en $70K y el 97% de altcoins en rojo es difícil ver más allá. Pero lo que está pasand
company.description:
Sé que con BTC en $70K y el 97% de altcoins en rojo es difícil ver más allá. Pero lo que está pasando debajo del ruido de precios es, posiblemente, lo más importante del ciclo.

Anchorage Digital, el único banco con licencia federal cripto en EEUU (respaldado Goldman,Visa...), acaba de integrar acceso directo a Morpho, Aave, Lido y más de 50 protocolos DeFi a través de su wallet institucional. 

Hasta ahora, un fondo de pensiones o una tesorería corporativa que quisiera yield en DeFi tenía un problema serio: no podían. Su compliance se lo prohibía. Al no haber custodio instucional, era imposible.

Ese muro se está cayendo. Coinbase ya lanzó préstamos respaldados por crypto via Morpho. Bitwise, con $15B bajo gestión, ya es vault curator en Morpho ofreciendo ~6% APY en stablecoins. https://t.co/OmmZujUOBy integró lending via Morpho. Y ahora Anchorage abre la puerta a todo su libro de clientes institucionales.

Los números de Morpho hablan solos: de 67K a 1.4M usuarios en 2025, depósitos de $5B a $13B, préstamos activos en $4.5B, y $400M en RWAs tokenizados. Es el segundo protocolo de lending más grande, ya en 29 cadenas.

Como siempre, el capital institucional no llega en ATH cuando todo el mundo mira. Llega en silencio, a través de infraestructura regulada, custodia cualificada y productos que encajan con sus mandatos de compliance. Eso es exactamente lo que se está construyendo ahora.

Los precios nos están diciendo que cripto está muerto. 

La infraestructura nos está diciendo que es el mejor momento para encontrar proyectos ganadores.

company.title:
1. The Core Philosophy: "Bitcoin Stays Blind"

In standard bridges (like WBTC), there is a "Multisig
company.description:
1. The Core Philosophy: "Bitcoin Stays Blind"

In standard bridges (like WBTC), there is a "Multisig Wallet" on the Bitcoin network controlled by 5-10 entities (like BitGo). You have to trust them.

Alienc0der is saying: "Bitcoin should not verify the other chain (Zenon). Bitcoin must remain blind."
To the Bitcoin network, the transaction looks like a standard signature spend. Bitcoin does not say, "This transaction happened because tokens were burned on Zenon"; it simply says, "The signature is valid, transaction approved."

2. What is Witness Encryption?

This is the heart of the system.

Normally, to encrypt data, you need a Person (Public Key).

In Witness Encryption, you encrypt data to a Fact (NP Statement).

Example: I put Bitcoin in a box and program the lock as follows: "This lock will open if and only if a 'Burn Proof' (Witness) containing a specific transaction hash from the Zenon Network is presented."

The thing that opens the box is not a "Person" (Admin, Multisig member), but a Mathematical Proof.If that proof (Witness) exists, the encryption dissolves, and the Bitcoin is released. If the proof doesn't exist, all the computers in the universe combined cannot move that Bitcoin.

3. The Two Variants

Alienc0der mentions two different implementation methods here:

Variant A (Recommended - Signature Release):

Here, the "Private Key" is not encrypted.
Instead, the Signature of a pre-constructed Bitcoin transaction is encrypted.

Scenario: User burns zBTC on Zenon -> Generates Proof (Witness) -> Uses this proof to decrypt the package -> The package reveals only the signature required to execute that specific transaction.

Security: Even if the person decrypting it is malicious, the revealed signature only says "Send 1 BTC to User X." They cannot change it to "Send to User Y." At worst, they broadcast the transaction for everyone (which is what you want anyway).

Variant B (Obfuscated Contract):

A more complex method involving an "Obfuscated Smart Contract" (Smart Secret) that never reveals the key but outputs the signature. This is discussed more in Ethereum research circles (Suegami's research), but Variant A is cleaner and safer for Zenon.

4. The Implication for Zenon: "Programmability in Cryptography"

Alienc0der’s following sentence is critical:

"Programmability lives in cryptography, not Script"

Bitcoin's language (Script) is constrained ("No loops, no smart contracts"). Bitcoin L2s usually say, "Then let's change Bitcoin" (OP_CAT, covenants, etc.). Zenon says, "No, leave Bitcoin alone. We will embed the programmability into the Cryptography (Witness Encryption)."

In Summary: 
With this system, Zenon aims to become the first network to manage Bitcoin without the need for a Custodian. 
To convert Bitcoin to Zenon (zBTC), you don't trust a company; you trust mathematics (encrypted witness). If you burn zBTC on Zenon, the lock on the Bitcoin network opens automatically. There is no human in the middle, only the Witness.

company.text:
1. The Core Philosophy: "Bitcoin Stays Blind"

In standard bridges (like WBTC), there is a "Multisig Wallet" on the Bitcoin network controlled by 5-10 entities (like BitGo). You have to trust them.

Alienc0der is saying: "Bitcoin should not verify the other chain (Zenon). Bitcoin must remain blind."
To the Bitcoin network, the transaction looks like a standard signature spend. Bitcoin does not say, "This transaction happened because tokens were burned on Zenon"; it simply says, "The signature is valid, transaction approved."

2. What is Witness Encryption?

This is the heart of the system.

Normally, to encrypt data, you need a Person (Public Key).

In Witness Encryption, you encrypt data to a Fact (NP Statement).

Example: I put Bitcoin in a box and program the lock as follows: "This lock will open if and only if a 'Burn Proof' (Witness) containing a specific transaction hash from the Zenon Network is presented."

The thing that opens the box is not a "Person" (Admin, Multisig member), but a Mathematical Proof.If that proof (Witness) exists, the encryption dissolves, and the Bitcoin is released. If the proof doesn't exist, all the computers in the universe combined cannot move that Bitcoin.

3. The Two Variants

Alienc0der mentions two different implementation methods here:

Variant A (Recommended - Signature Release):

Here, the "Private Key" is not encrypted.
Instead, the Signature of a pre-constructed Bitcoin transaction is encrypted.

Scenario: User burns zBTC on Zenon -> Generates Proof (Witness) -> Uses this proof to decrypt the package -> The package reveals only the signature required to execute that specific transaction.

Security: Even if the person decrypting it is malicious, the revealed signature only says "Send 1 BTC to User X." They cannot change it to "Send to User Y." At worst, they broadcast the transaction for everyone (which is what you want anyway).

Variant B (Obfuscated Contract):

A more complex method involving an "Obfuscated Smart Contract" (Smart Secret) that never reveals the key but outputs the signature. This is discussed more in Ethereum research circles (Suegami's research), but Variant A is cleaner and safer for Zenon.

4. The Implication for Zenon: "Programmability in Cryptography"

Alienc0der’s following sentence is critical:

"Programmability lives in cryptography, not Script"

Bitcoin's language (Script) is constrained ("No loops, no smart contracts"). Bitcoin L2s usually say, "Then let's change Bitcoin" (OP_CAT, covenants, etc.). Zenon says, "No, leave Bitcoin alone. We will embed the programmability into the Cryptography (Witness Encryption)."
